newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN plans airdropping food to east Zaire refugees.
newsitem.headline: UN plans airdropping food to east Zaire refugees.

text.p: A huge airlift for Rwandan Hutu refugees fleeing Tutsi rebels in east Zaire may start before the end of the week, with the remote Zairean outpost of Kisangani serving as a key base, senior U.N. officials said on Tuesday.

Details of the plan emerged as Canada said it was ready to command a multinational force in Zaire to protect the relief operation and U.N. officials said the force could be on the ground as early as this weekend.

Racing against the clock to save the lives of a million Rwandan refugees and displaced Zaireans facing disease and starvation, aid agencies and U.N. refugee agency officials urgently met in Geneva to discuss the airlift.

Flying thousands of tonnes of fuel, food, blankets and supplies to the obscure town of Kisangani, the last outpost of tenuous Zairean authority before a wilderness of forest and hills, will cost a fortune and is likely to be a logistical nightmare, U.N. officials said.
Under the plan, the airlift would be supported by military planes and helicopters, they said.
"Kisangani will be the main centre for distribution of aid. It will be a huge operation," said a U.N. official.
"Bringing food and supplies to Kisangani will create a lot of problems. That's why we are considering using military helicopters and planes," he added but gave no details.

Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes said the U.N. might give a green light within 48 hours to the deployment of a multinational force in eastern Zaire but details have yet to emerge on where and how it will operate.

Western aid officials said a U.N. fact-finding team was on its way to Kisangani, 500 km (310 miles) from eastern Zaire's volatile Goma border region, to assess the situation on the ground and tackle the complex issue of how to reach the scattered refugees.
U.N. officials said emergency food and relief supplies would be airlifted to Kisangani from regional airports in the Kenyan capital Nairobi and Uganda's Kampala.
Under the plan, small planes would do overflights to locate the refugees and helicopters would airdrop food for refugees in areas inaccessible by road, they said.
"The helicopters could be operational by next week. We could reach the refugees from the west. There will be airdrops," said a U.N. refugee agency official.

The focus of the airlift has moved deeper into Zaire and away from Goma after bureaucratic formalities by suspicious ethnic Tutsi Banyamulenge Tutsi rebels prevented a U.N. fact-finding mission from distributing aid for a second say in a row, U.N. officials said.
More than half a million mostly Rwandan Hutu refugees fled their camps outside Rwanda's borders after the Rwandan-backed rebels seized large swathes of eastern Zaire.
